why_this_exists: The figure '28 published artifacts, no route to a buyer, ¥0 in eight months' is asserted in state/zerobase.json, state/eta.json, state/predictions.json, state/constraints.json and a comment in scripts/repricing.mjs. It entered at 8eca5b1 (2026-08-09T10:27:30Z) with no source and nothing ever enumerated it. It is load-bearing: it is the evidence that publishing-and-waiting has already been run 28 times, which is what demotes every build candidate. A number doing that much work should have a list under it.
what_was_counted_here: Two independent enumerations, both taken 2026-08-09T11:12Z, both complete rather than sampled.

items.immediately_tryable: UNRESOLVED, and previously overstated. This said 'yes' on the strength of the title and a sibling public repository. It was measured on 2026-08-09 and the measurement cannot decide it — see public_reachability_measured. Separately and certainly: the page is served noindex,nofollow, so it is never findable, only linkable.

public_reachability_measured.method: unauthenticated GET from this session, plus a control
public_reachability_measured.what_came_back: HTTP 200, 14019 bytes, a generic single-page shell. og:title is 'Claude Artifact', not the artifact's title, and none of the game's strings appear in the served HTML. The content is rendered by JavaScript after load.
public_reachability_measured.the_control_that_makes_this_decisive: The same GET against 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000, a UUID that cannot exist, returned HTTP 200 at exactly 14019 bytes with a byte-identical shell — the only differences are the echoed data-frame-uuid and the CSP nonce. So status code, response size and HTML all carry ZERO information about whether an artifact exists, let alone whether a stranger can open it.
public_reachability_measured.verdict: NOT public, and NOT private — undecidable from here by this method. The earlier 'immediately_tryable: yes' rested on the title and on a sibling repository, never on opening the page, and this measurement does not rescue it.
public_reachability_measured.what_would_decide_it: a JavaScript-executing client carrying no claude.ai session. state/constraints.json playwright_cannot_reach_external says that is unavailable here, so this is not merely undone — it is not doable from this environment.
public_reachability_measured.the_finding_that_does_not_depend_on_reac: the shell is served with <meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">, twice. Even if the artifact is fully public, it can never be found through a search engine. It works only as a link someone is handed. Any plan that expected the free demo to be discovered on its own is refuted by this line regardless of how the privacy question resolves.

enumerations.contents_note: Names only. Whether these are published, playable, or abandoned scratch repositories was NOT checked. Counting a repository as a published artifact is exactly the sort of inflation this file exists to stop, so they are listed, not totalled into a headline figure.

against_the_28.verdict: unsupported by anything enumerable from here, and NOT thereby refuted
against_the_28.detail: 5 published artifacts and 14 repositories. state/itch.json reports 0 games; state/gumroad.json reports product_count 1 and 0 lifetime sales. No combination of these reaches 28.
against_the_28.the_honest_gap: The private youtube repository holds figures this environment cannot read — state/external-metrics.json has never been published, which is already recorded as a wiring exception. If '28' counted published videos, it could be right and unverifiable from here. So this entry does not say the number is wrong. It says the number has no list under it and the lists that do exist do not add up to it.
against_the_28.what_would_settle_it: publish state/external-metrics.json from the repository that holds the YouTube credentials, or have whoever wrote 8eca5b1 name what was counted. Until then, treat 28 as an assertion, not an observation.

the_priced_artifact.why_this_was_added: This file enumerated free artifacts and repository names and then asked whether any of it reaches BUYERS. It never listed the one artifact that has a price. state/gumroad.json has been collected hourly the whole time and carries exactly one published product; nothing in this file mentioned it. A portfolio that omits the only thing with a price cannot answer a question about buyers.
the_priced_artifact.source: api.gumroad.com/v2/products, read directly at 11:27Z with the token this environment already holds. The hourly collector had been reading the same endpoint all along and keeping only counts, so the descriptive fields were never stored and nobody had looked at them.
the_priced_artifact.what_it_is: A rebrandable browser idle-clicker, sold as a commercial licence. Plain HTML/CSS/JS, no build step, no external libraries, no network calls, saves on the device. One config file decides title, palette, the name of the thing being counted, the generators, the upgrades, the milestone text, the call-to-action button and the footer. It ships a form-based config generator, three worked rebrands, a config validator and a browser test script. Name, price and sales counts stay in state/gumroad.json rather than being copied here.
the_priced_artifact.licence_terms_as_written: one publishing destination, for the buyer own shop, company or channel; commercial use and modification allowed. Delivering it inside client work is by separate arrangement. Reselling or redistributing the kit itself as a template product is prohibited.

who_it_actually_addresses.the_pitch_as_written: give your customers a reason to open your site again
who_it_actually_addresses.what_this_corrects: codex task 2026-08-09.k was dispatched at 11:26Z describing the buyer class as people who buy game source code or production kits with a commercial licence, i.e. developers. That is the wrong class. The product is not sold to people who want to make a game; it is sold to people who want a small branded thing on their own site so customers come back. Those two audiences gather in different places, so the venue half of that survey is aimed off-target.
who_it_actually_addresses.what_follows: the venue and rule questions in .k (questions 2 and 3) are buyer-class-independent and still worth the run. Question 1 and question 4 are not, and need re-asking against the corrected class. Do not read the .k answer for question 1 or 4 without this note next to it.

the_pair_this_makes.claim: there is a free, immediately-playable artifact of the same genre AND a priced product, so the shape codex/outbox/2026-08-09.i.md found in every fast first-sale case is already assembled: a finished thing the reader can try at once, with something purchasable behind it.
the_pair_this_makes.status: PARTLY VERIFIED. The paid side is now read from the API rather than inferred: it is an idle-clicker kit, and the stack matches the free browser build. What is still unverified is whether the free build is literally the same codebase as what the kit ships.
the_pair_this_makes.why_the_remaining_gap_may_not_matter: the funnel needs a demo of the same genre and stack that a reader can try in one click. Same-code identity would be tidier, but the demo works either way.
the_pair_this_makes.what_would_verify_it: compare the free build against the kit contents. The kit is a small download; nobody has done this.

the_priced_artifact.what_it_changes_about_the_open_question: Whether a free browser idle game has buyers was the wrong question to send outward. Players of a free idle game are not buyers, which this file already said. The priced product is not aimed at players and not aimed at developers either — it is aimed at small operators who want a retention widget on their own site. That is the class whose gathering places need naming.
the_priced_artifact.still_not_established: that anyone buys this. Zero lifetime sales is a measurement, and state/eta.json channels.gumroad already records why: no traffic source feeds it. This entry does not claim the product is good or priced right. It claims the enumeration was incomplete, the buy link was missing from the file that tracks the product, and the outward question named the wrong buyer.

the_question_this_was_actually_opened_fo.question: Is there a finished artifact a reader could try immediately? codex/outbox/2026-08-09.i.md found that in every fast first-sale case there was one, and that no case succeeded on a bare announcement. state/zerobase.json recorded honest_post_where_buyers_gather as blocked_on 'there is nothing to post about yet', and the previous handoff recorded that nobody had ever looked.
the_question_this_was_actually_opened_fo.answer: Yes, at least one. The cookie-clicker idle game is free, browser-playable and corroborated by a second source. Two more artifacts are games and are probably tryable, though neither page was opened.
the_question_this_was_actually_opened_fo.so_the_blocker_moves: honest_post_where_buyers_gather was not blocked on having something to post. That half is answered and it was cheap — one tool call. What it is actually blocked on is the other half, which is still untouched: whether any of these reaches a community that contains BUYERS. A free browser idle game has players, and players are not the same as buyers. Do not read this entry as saying the route is now open.
the_question_this_was_actually_opened_fo.do_not_overclaim: Nobody has established that any of these five is worth posting. Established: something postable exists. Those are different sentences and the difference is the whole remaining question.
